five_requirements.name: Conformance Level
five_requirements.rule: All applicable success criteria at or below the declared level must be satisfied or a conforming alternate version supplied; A and AA are cumulative.
five_requirements.review_evidence: Criterion outcome matrix, functional alternatives, review notes and no unresolved failures.

five_requirements.name: Full Pages
five_requirements.rule: Conformance is of complete web pages, not isolated widgets or selected sections.
five_requirements.review_evidence: Defined URLs/page types and evidence for headers, footer, embedded content, overlays and other complete-page content.

five_requirements.name: Complete Processes
five_requirements.rule: All pages in a multi-page process must conform at the declared level.
five_requirements.review_evidence: End-to-end task map and test of every step including error, empty, timeout and completion states.

five_requirements.name: Only Accessibility-Supported Ways of Using Technologies
five_requirements.rule: The ways of using technologies relied upon must be accessibility supported; otherwise equivalent accessible pathways must provide information and functions.
five_requirements.review_evidence: Supported browser and assistive technology combinations and evidence for relied-upon patterns.

five_requirements.name: Non-Interference
five_requirements.rule: Unsupported or nonconforming content must not block use of the rest of the page. 1.4.2, 2.1.2, 2.3.1, 2.2.2 apply to all content, even content not relied upon.
five_requirements.review_evidence: Inspect third-party content, media, moving widgets and keyboard traps even outside the relied-upon alternate.

claims.caution: Skill output and automated scanner results do not independently establish a formal conformance claim.

scope_notes: Do not infer jurisdiction-specific legal compliance from W3C conformance.
Record not-applicable separately from pass, with evidence.
Do not treat not-tested, needs-manual-review or a passing automated scan as success.
Do not make whole-site claims from sampled pages without transparent methodology and appropriate assurance.
4.1.1 in the current WCAG 2.1 recommendation is considered always satisfied for HTML/XML; meaningful accessibility impact must be mapped to other criteria.
